from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import io
import os

import pytest
import requests


@pytest.fixture
def url():
    return os.getenv("SITE", "http://localhost:5000")


@pytest.fixture
def image_bytes():
    img = Image.new("RGB", (100, 100), color="red")
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    draw.text((10, 10), "Hi!", fill="blue")
    byte_array = io.BytesIO()
    img.save(byte_array, format="jpeg")
    yield byte_array.getvalue()


def test_post_images(expect, url):
    params = {"key": "iw", "lines": ["test", "deployment"]}
    response = requests.post(f"{url}/api/images", json=params)
    expect(response.status_code) == 201
    expect(response.json()["url"]).endswith("/api/images/iw/test/deployment.png")


def test_get_image(expect, url):
    response = requests.get(f"{url}/iw/tests_code/in_production.jpg")
    expect(response.status_code) == 200
    expect(response.headers["Content-Type"]) == "image/jpeg"


def test_get_custom_image(expect, url, image_bytes):
    with open("in_production.jpg", "wb") as f:
        f.write(image_bytes)
    file = {"file": ("custom.jpg", open("in_production.jpg", "rb"), "image/jpeg")}
    response = requests.put(f"{url}/api/images/iw/custom.jpg", files=file)
    expect(response.status_code) == 200

    response = requests.get(f"{url}/iw/custom.jpg")
    expect(response.status_code) == 200
    expect(response.headers["Content-Type"]) == "image/jpeg"

import base64
import os

import pytest
import requests


@pytest.fixture
def url():
    return os.getenv("SITE", "http://localhost:5000")


def test_post_images(expect, url):
    params = {"key": "iw", "lines": ["test", "deployment"]}
    response = requests.post(f"{url}/api/images", json=params)
    expect(response.status_code) == 201
    expect(response.json()["url"]).endswith("/api/images/iw/test/deployment.png")


def test_get_image(expect, url):
    response = requests.get(f"{url}/iw/tests_code/in_production.jpg")
    expect(response.status_code) == 200
    expect(response.headers["Content-Type"]) == "image/jpeg"


def test_get_custom_image_encoding(expect, url):
    with open("./tests/code/in_production.jpg", "rb") as image_file:
        encoded_string = base64.b64encode(image_file.read())

    response = requests.put(
        f"{url}/iw/tests_code/in_production.jpg", data=encoded_string
    )
    expect(response.status_code) == 200

    response = requests.get(f"{url}/iw/tests_code/in_production.jpg")
    expect(response.status_code) == 200
    content = base64.b64decode(response.content)
    expect(content) == encoded_string
    expect(response.headers["Content-Type"]) == "image/jpeg"

from nova.scheduler import filters
from openstackxenapi.common import utils


class TripleOCapabilitiesFilter(filters.BaseHostFilter):
    """Filter hosts based on capabilities in boot request

    The standard Nova ComputeCapabilitiesFilter does not respect capabilities
    requested in the scheduler_hints field, so we need a custom one in order
    to be able to do predictable placement of nodes.

    Note that this filter currently does not behave quite like the provided
    ComputeCapabilitiesFilter in that it does not support lists of valid
    host nodes.  It also doesn't need to be disabled using
    disabled_filters since it doesn't have a null_result.

    """

    # list of hosts doesn't change within a request
    run_filter_once_per_request = True

    def host_passes(self, host_state, spec_obj):
        host_node = host_state.stats.get('node')
        instance_node = spec_obj.scheduler_hints.get('capabilities:node')
        LOG = utils.get_request_logger(spec_obj)
        # The instance didn't request a specific node
        if not instance_node:
            return True

        if len(instance_node) == 1 and host_node == instance_node[0]:
            return True

        LOG.info('%s does not match requested node(s) %s',
                 host_node, instance_node)
        return False
